title: Soil organic cover and conservation agriculture
content: Maintaining organic soil cover with crop residues and cover crops can protect soil from erosion, contribute organic matter, support soil structure, and improve nutrient cycling. Vegetative cover can also provide habitat and resources for organisms within agricultural systems.

title: Conservation agriculture principles
content: Conservation agriculture is based on principles including minimum soil disturbance, permanent soil cover, and crop diversification. These practices are intended to improve soil condition, reduce degradation, and support more sustainable agricultural ecosystems.

title: Agroforestry and ecosystem services
content: Agroforestry integrates trees with crops or livestock and can provide multiple ecosystem services. Trees can contribute to soil protection, carbon storage, habitat provision, water regulation, and landscape connectivity.

title: Habitat diversity and biodiversity
content: Changes in land use and habitat simplification are important pressures on biodiversity. Maintaining diverse habitats can provide organisms with a wider range of resources, shelter, and ecological niches.

title: Land degradation, biodiversity and ecosystem services
content: Land-use change, land degradation, and unsustainable land management can affect terrestrial ecosystems, biodiversity, soil functions, and ecosystem services. Sustainable land management can help reduce degradation and support ecosystem functions.

title: Climate change impacts on terrestrial and freshwater ecosystems
content: Climate change affects terrestrial and freshwater ecosystems through changes in temperature, precipitation, extreme events, and other climate-related pressures. These changes can alter species distributions, ecological processes, and ecosystem functioning.

title: Drought and ecosystem impacts
content: Changes in drought frequency and intensity can increase water stress for ecosystems. Reduced water availability can affect vegetation productivity, species survival, and ecosystem functioning, particularly when combined with other environmental pressures.

title: Freshwater ecosystems and biodiversity
content: Freshwater availability and ecosystem condition are closely connected to biodiversity and ecosystem functioning. Protecting freshwater systems and maintaining ecological water conditions can support aquatic organisms and surrounding ecosystems.

title: Pollution as a biodiversity pressure
content: Pollution is one of the major direct drivers affecting biodiversity. Reducing harmful pollutants can decrease ecological stress and improve environmental conditions for organisms and ecosystems.

title: Ecosystem restoration and biodiversity
content: Ecosystem restoration can improve ecological condition by recovering degraded habitats, restoring ecological functions, and supporting biodiversity. Restoration approaches should consider local ecological conditions and the causes of degradation.

title: Soil biodiversity and soil functions
content: Soil organisms contribute to decomposition, nutrient cycling, soil structure, and other soil functions. Management practices that maintain organic matter and suitable soil conditions can support soil biodiversity and associated ecosystem functions.

title: Agriculture, water and climate resilience
content: Climate-related changes in temperature, rainfall, drought, and extreme events can affect agricultural ecosystems and water availability. Diversified and sustainable land management approaches can contribute to resilience while reducing environmental pressures.

title: Pollination and agricultural biodiversity
content: Pollinators are an important component of crop-associated biodiversity. Diverse agricultural systems can provide resources and habitat for pollinators, supporting pollination and associated ecosystem functions.

title: Biodiversity and natural pest regulation
content: Integrated pest management uses ecological processes and natural pest-control mechanisms while aiming to minimize disruption to agroecosystems. Predators and other beneficial organisms can contribute to biological pest regulation.

title: Crop genetic diversity and resilience
content: Crop genetic diversity can help maintain production and nutritional diversity across different agroecological conditions. Maintaining diverse crop genetic resources can contribute to adaptation and resilience under changing environmental conditions.

title: Crop diversification and ecosystem services
content: Evidence synthesized across many studies indicates that agricultural diversification can enhance biodiversity and ecosystem services including pollination, pest control, nutrient cycling, soil fertility, and water regulation. Outcomes can vary with context and management.

title: Soil organisms and nutrient cycling
content: Soil fauna and microorganisms contribute to decomposition, nutrient cycling, soil structure, and other soil functions. Maintaining biological diversity below ground is therefore an important component of healthy agroecosystems.

title: Agricultural intensification and biodiversity pressure
content: Intensive agricultural production can place pressure on land, water, biodiversity, and other natural resources. Reducing unnecessary environmental pressures and incorporating biodiversity-supporting management can improve ecological resilience.

title: Agroecology, biodiversity and climate resilience
content: Agroecology applies ecological principles to interactions among crops, animals, people, and the environment. Diversification and conservation of above- and below-ground biodiversity can support ecosystem services, sustainability, and resilience to climate change.

title: Climate-driven species range shifts
content: Climate warming has caused observed shifts in the geographic ranges of many animal and plant species. Range shifts can occur toward higher latitudes or elevations, while range contractions can increase risks to biodiversity and local populations.

title: Habitat loss and fragmentation
content: Habitat loss and land-use change are major pressures affecting species and ecosystems. Habitat conversion can interact with climate change and other pressures, influencing species survival, distribution, and ecosystem resilience.

title: Interactions among climate and human pressures
content: Climate change impacts on biodiversity can be compounded by habitat loss and fragmentation, pollution, water abstraction, nutrient enrichment, invasive species, and other human pressures. Multiple simultaneous pressures can increase vulnerability and reduce ecological resilience.

title: Species loss and ecosystem resilience
content: Loss of species can reduce ecosystem functioning and the ability of ecosystems to provide services. Biodiversity loss can also reduce resilience to climate-related pressures.

title: Agricultural diversification and multiple ecosystem services
content: A large synthesis of agricultural diversification studies found that diversification practices can improve above- and below-ground biodiversity and ecosystem services such as pollination, pest control, nutrient cycling, soil fertility, and water regulation. Effects vary depending on the practice and context.
